extraction.name: Science Question Answering (SCIENCE QA)
extraction.description: A new benchmark that consists of 21k multimodal multiple choice questions with diverse science topics and annotations of their answers with corresponding lectures and explanations.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.publisher: 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors downloaded science problems from an online learning platform, extracted components using heuristic rules, manually removed invalid or duplicated questions, shuffled answer options, reformatted texts using semi-automated scripts, and had experts manually revise incorrect annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of K-12 science problems, including questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions, sourced from the IXL Learning online platform and aligned with California Common Core Content Standards.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples in the collected dataset were reviewed using a custom data exploration tool, and any incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts to ensure data quality.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used as a benchmark to diagnose the multi-hop reasoning ability and interpretability of AI systems, specifically to study if language models can generate reasonable explanations and improve reasoning ability.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code are released and made available via a dedicated GitHub project website.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Missing context text for questions is imputed by replacing it with an empty string.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The answer options for each question were shuffled to prevent pattern recognition, and the dataset was randomly split into training, validation, and test sets with a 60:20:20 ratio.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning involved manually removing invalid, faulty, or duplicated questions, and keeping only one correct answer if multiple applied. Lectures and solutions were reformatted using semi-automated scripts. Additionally, newline characters were replaced with escaped newlines for language model encoding.
